subject: HealthSync discovery — recommended runtime & verified perf pack
messages:
From: Asha Mehta <asha@healthsync.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.ai, Devindra Rao <devindra@healthsync.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery — HealthSync inference priorities

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope a clean pilot:

- Primary workload: summarization + structured extraction from multi-section clinical notes (avg 850 tokens, peaks ~3k).
- Must-haves: p99 latency <= 450ms for interactive reviewer flows; sustained TPS for batch ingest ~18 TPS during nightly windows.
- Quality constraints: extremely low hallucination tolerance on medication and allergies fields.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and data retention options required by procurement.

Can you share recommended models + perf expectations (TPS, p50/p90/p99 latency) and any sample prompt sets you’d want to test? Procurement also asked for a tentative cost estimate per 1M tokens.

Best,
Asha
Asha Mehta
Head of Product, HealthSync AI
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — HealthSync inference priorities

Thanks Asha — great notes. Quick post-call recap and an initial recommendation set so your team can review before we lock a pilot scope. (Forwarding below for context.)

Summary / immediate recs:
- Recommended starting slate: Redwood-mistral-8k-q4 (quantized), Redwood-llama2-13b-int8, and an experiment with Redwood-flare-7b (low-latency).
  - Why these: balance between factuality for extraction (13b) and latency/cost for reviewer flows (7b/8k quantized).
- Verified perf snapshot (attached CSV & Drive link): per-model sustained TPS and latency percentiles measured on n1-standard equivalent with continuous batching configured to your sequence profile. Key lines pulled out below:
  - Redwood-mistral-8k-q4 — sustained TPS: 22 TPS; p50: 85ms; p90: 210ms; p99: 390ms
  - Redwood-llama2-13b-int8 — sustained TPS: 12 TPS; p50: 120ms; p90: 300ms; p99: 520ms
  - Redwood-flare-7b — sustained TPS: 30 TPS; p50: 60ms; p90: 150ms; p99: 270ms

Notes on quality/regression risk:
- Extraction fidelity is model-dependent. We’ve seen occasional entity linking regressions when prompts over-index on conversational framing vs structured extraction. We recommend a regression guardrail set (sample prompts + failure cases) before any rollout.

Attachments provided: redwood-verified-perfpack-20260917.csv (full traces), hs-promptset-v1.txt (starter prompt templates), healthsync-cost-estimate-draft.pdf (ballpark tokens-to-cost). Also uploaded the perfpack to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/HealthSync/PerfPack/verified-perfpack-20260917

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) to align on sequence distribution and sampling prompts — propose Tue 2026-09-21 10:00 or Wed 2026-09-22 15:00 PT.
2) Ben will prepare a short targeted run with your top-20 clinical notes (anonymized) to capture hallucination surface and end-to-end latency.
3) Procurement: we’ll share SOC 2 evidence and a simple procurement checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted options.

If that looks good I’ll lock the TD with Ben and Jonas on our side.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Mateo: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@healthsync.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — HealthSync inference priorities

Asha / team —

I’ll own the TD and the initial test run. Deliverables from our side:
- One-run perf traces for the three candidate models (attached trace CSV excerpt).
- A tailored prompt pack (attached hs-promptset-v1.txt) with structured extraction templates and negative examples to probe hallucination.
- Quick regression checklist: token-level diff, entity-consistency checks, and a small post-hoc ruleset (if desired) to hard-fail obviously inconsistent medication entries.

Quality concern to call out: on very long notes (>>2k tokens) we’ve seen entity-context bleed where models drift across earlier sections; this impacts p99 and extraction fidelity. For the pilot I recommend:
- enforce max chunk window + overlap strategy, and
- include a small eval set with ground-truth extractions (20–30 records) for early regression alerts.

Attachments: hs-promptset-v1.txt (8 templates + negative cases), run-traces-excerpt.csv (perf excerpt).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Devindra Rao <devindra@healthsync.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Mehta <asha@healthsync.ai>, procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: 2026-09-16T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — HealthSync inference priorities

Thanks Mateo & Ben — this is helpful. A couple quick asks from product + procurement:
1) Can you include TPS numbers at 95th percentile (not just sustained) — procurement is sensitive to peak behavior during nightly batches.
2) Can you provide a 1M-token hosted cost estimate and a separate number for Dedicated (monthly commit)? Your draft PDF is a good start but procurement needs the Dedicated delta.
3) SOC 2 evidence & data residency options — procurement will flag the requirement if we scope a pilot.

Also we can confirm an anonymized sample set for the run. We’re aiming for the TD on Tue 2026-09-21 10:00 PT.

—Devindra
Director, Engineering | HealthSync AI

Subject: Re: Discovery — HealthSync inference priorities

Perfect — thanks for the clarifying asks. Short answers and next actions: 

- 95th percentile TPS/latency: included in the attached CSV (columns: tps_95, latency_p95). Snapshot highlights:
  - Redwood-mistral-8k-q4 — tps_95: 26 TPS; p95 latency: 270ms
  - Redwood-llama2-13b-int8 — tps_95: 14 TPS; p95 latency: 360ms
  - Redwood-flare-7b — tps_95: 34 TPS; p95 latency: 170ms

- Cost estimates: see healthsync-cost-estimate-draft.pdf (attached). Quick summary: hosted (1M tokens): $62 (mixed slate, typical prompt/response split); Dedicated (1-month commit, baseline): ~ $6,800 — exact depends on committed qps and model mix. We’ll follow up with a Dedicated delta sheet for procurement.

- SOC 2 & data residency: attaching a SOC2 evidence pointer and a short procurement checklist in Drive. I’ll loop Security for any signed NDA/Evidence transfer.

Action items: 
1) Confirm TD time Tue 2026-09-21 10:00 PT (calendar invite pending).
2) HealthSync: share anonymized sample set via secure upload link (I’ll send a signed upload token + instructions).
3) Redwood: Ben and Jonas will run a targeted job and share perf traces + a small regression report within 48 hours of receiving samples.
4) Procurement: we’ll send Dedicated delta + SOC2 package by EOD 2026-09-17.
